decisions.reason: As an adjacent psychiatric service with strong fit to existing clinical capabilities and likely still-unresolved demand potential, its option value remains higher than the cost of continuing it.

The carpentry workshop fits the firm's therapeutic and production know-how, but its more asset- and market-intensive profile raises carrying costs, so it is kept with moderate exit risk while management learns more.
Outpatient sociotherapy is close to the core support offer and relatively flexible to run, so the firm is likely to preserve this low-cost option until clearer evidence arrives.
Counseling for senior living is highly aligned with the firm's eldercare activities and appears strategically important and inexpensive to sustain, making withdrawal unlikely.

The retail shop supports the sheltered-workshop logic but faces more commercial uncertainty and ongoing operating costs, so it is kept for now though it has the highest near-term chance of being discontinued.
